Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

timestralR (development version)

  • timestral_backtest() runs a rolling-origin backtest: it forecasts from a sequence of origins using only the data up to each one (with covariates and the observation mask cut to match), and returns one scored row per origin, series, variate and step. timestral_score() scores any forecast against realised values: absolute error of the median, pinball loss averaged over the levels, CRPS approximated from the quantiles (trapezoidal over the knots), and interval coverage. Both are single-threaded; ?timestral_backtest shows how to split origins across parallel workers. With the native backend, origins that differ by a multiple of the patch size (32 for the official checkpoints) reuse the K/V cache over the context they share, which roughly halves a long-series backtest with such a step (1.30 to 0.63 s for 12 origins on 28M).

  • The native K/V cache keeps two entries (the forward and mirrored passes of a symmetric forecast no longer evict each other) and reuses the longest run of leading patches a context shares with a cached one, rather than only an exact extension of it.

  • timestral_supports_covariates() and timestral_supports_known_covariates() report which covariates a checkpoint can condition on (the Python forecaster’s supports_covariates/supports_known_covariates), and printing a model shows the same.

  • predict() method for timestral_model: predict(m, newdata, h) is timestral_forecast(m, newdata, h) and returns the same timestral_forecast.

  • forecast package interface (forecast in Suggests): timestral_as_forecast() converts a forecast from ts input to a "forecast" object, and forecast::forecast(m, y, h) forecasts and converts in one call, so accuracy(), autoplot() and the rest of the forecast package work. Interval bounds are read off the quantile knots, never interpolated; the default levels are 80% and 98% because the official knots have no 2.5%/97.5% quantiles.

  • Printing a forecast reports the checkpoint’s number of quantile levels rather than always 21.

  • timestral_load() and timestral_download() accept any Hugging Face Hub repository ID ("owner/name") holding a Timestral checkpoint, for example a fine-tuned model, as well as the four sizes. The official repositories ("mistralai/Timestral-5M", …) keep their pinned, hash-verified commits however they are named. Branch and tag revisions are resolved to their current commit on the Hub and the resolution is cached for local_files_only use, so a moving branch such as "main" no longer stays frozen at its first download. Both functions gain a token argument (default: the HF_TOKEN environment variable).

  • The first argument of timestral_download() is renamed from size to model, matching timestral_load(). Positional calls are unaffected; calls written as size = "5M" must use model = "5M".

  • Forecasts take their quantile levels (fc$levels and the level dimnames) from the checkpoint’s quantile_knots instead of always using timestral_levels(), so checkpoints with other knots are labelled correctly; symmetric = TRUE now errors for knots that are not symmetric about 0.5, as upstream does, instead of silently averaging mismatched levels. plot() scales its y axis to the outermost knots rather than requiring 0.01 and 0.99.

  • Licence field tightened to Apache License (== 2.0), the licence of the upstream ‘timestral’ package the code is ported from, and Mistral AI is credited as copyright holder of the ported code.

  • The tiny random-weight test checkpoint now ships in inst/extdata/tiny, so every example except the downloads runs offline under R CMD check.

timestralR 0.5.0

  • Input validation hardening: timestral_forecast() now errors (instead of aborting the R session, hanging, or silently coercing) on empty or zero-dimension y, on a series with no finite observed values, on non-numeric y or covariates (character, factor, complex, Date, …), and on a horizon that is not a single whole number in [1, 10000]. The native .ts_load() re-validates the checkpoint config (positive patch_size/num_heads/block_size, d_model divisible by num_heads, valid rope_dim, increasing quantile knots containing 0.5), and .ts_predict_block() validates its dimensions, masks and id arguments. Parallel checkpoint downloads no longer collide: each download writes to a unique .part file and a lost rename race against an identical published file is accepted.
  • tidyverts support (all via Suggests, no new hard dependencies): tsibble input to timestral_forecast() (keys become the batch, measured variables the jointly forecast variates; tsibble covariates supported) and a tsibble::as_tsibble() method for forecasts; ggplot2::autoplot()/autolayer() fan-chart methods; and a fable interface — a TIMESTRAL() model definition for fabletools::model() (univariate response, per-key contexts, 21-quantile distributional forecasts) plus a fabletools::as_fable() method converting forecasts to fbl_ts. S3 methods for these generics are registered conditionally when the owning package is loaded.
  • Fixes to the tidyverts interfaces: as_tsibble()/as_fable() keep the index column for ts, zoo and xts forecasts (named index, and for ts with the yearmonth/yearquarter/… class that tsibble::as_tsibble() uses) and for tsibble indexes named time or step; multivariate forecasts convert to a fable with a variate key; quantile distributions are built in a way that works across distributional versions. Fitted TIMESTRAL() models store a handle to the checkpoint instead of the weights, so mables stay small when saved and forecast in new sessions or parallel workers. Tsibble inputs are put in index order and implicit gaps are filled with missing values; logical tsibbles work as observation masks; keyed tsibble covariates are matched to series by key and validated like other covariates. Plots label variates by name.
  • Documentation and NAMESPACE are generated with roxygen2; methods for ggplot2, tsibble and fabletools generics are registered through delayed S3method() entries instead of .onLoad hooks. DESCRIPTION now states Depends: R (>= 4.1.0) (the code uses the base pipe |>; tools::R_user_dir() needs only 4.0.0), and SystemRequirements states a C++17 compiler.
  • Checkpoint downloads are pinned to recorded upstream commits and verified against recorded SHA-256 hashes (new digest import); revision = NULL (the default in timestral_download() and timestral_load()) selects the pinned commit, a cached file that fails verification is re-downloaded, and failed downloads no longer leave .part files behind.
  • The native backend is split from one file into per-unit headers and implementation files (session, nn_ops, scaler, masks, attention, transformer, head, predict, plus the Rcpp entry points); outputs are bit-for-bit unchanged.
  • New vignette, vignette("timestralR"), covering every feature with plots (precomputed from vignettes/timestralR.Rmd.orig; rebuild with vignettes/precompile.R).
  • autoplot()/autolayer() draw opaque bands in graded blues, widest first, matching plot() (any fill scale still overrides them), and facet variates in input order. A list of series that share a time index keeps it, and a named list no longer leaks a name into dim().

timestralR 0.4.0

  • R workflow support: forecasts keep the observed history and the time index. ts/mts, zoo and xts inputs (the latter two via Suggests, no new hard dependency) preserve their index; the forecast object gains observed, index and future_index (extending the last observed interval), as_forecast_df() reports real index values (e.g. Dates), and covariates with a time index are checked for alignment with y. timestral_median()/timestral_quantile() now return a ts/mts for a single-series ts forecast.
  • New plot() method for forecasts: fan chart with the observed context, median, and 50/80/90/98% predictive bands.
  • Documentation: examples in every help page, a package-level help page, and URL/BugReports in DESCRIPTION.

timestralR 0.3.1

  • Native backend speedups, no change to results (native vs R backend still agrees to < 1e-10 on the fixtures; multi-block decode on 209M agrees to ~4e-13): context K/V cached across decode blocks, rows batched into single GEMMs, fused attention with head-block QKV layout and mask-as-bias, and activations kept in one stacked matrix through the transformer. The native backend remains single-threaded by design (see docs/developer-notes.md).
  • Speed on this machine (209M): batch of 10 4.6 s -> 2.3 s, long-context 6.4 s -> 5.0 s, long horizon 1.7 s -> 1.3 s.

timestralR 0.3.0

  • Native RcppEigen backend (default, backend = "native" in timestral_load()): the single-block transformer primitive runs in C++ with Eigen, with large products routed to the system BLAS and small ones kept in Eigen (threshold tuned by benchmark; the tuned BLAS is not always faster). The pure-R implementation remains as backend = "R", the reference and fallback. Results agree to < 1e-10 on the golden fixtures; official parity is unchanged.
  • Speed on this machine: 209M long-context case 13.8 s (R) -> 6.4 s (native); 5M 0.80 s -> 0.22 s.

timestralR 0.2.0

  • Complete parity with the Python timestral package: batched series (list or 3-D array input), observation_mask, categorical past/known covariates with target encoding, and the forecaster/loader options per_shot_horizon_patches, quantile_real_cap_k, extreme_value_threshold, revision, cache_dir, local_files_only.
  • New accessors timestral_median() and timestral_quantile().
  • Config validation and strict weight checking at load, matching upstream; checkpoints with biases or non-default gates/schedules are supported.
  • Breaking: max_context now defaults to the checkpoint’s trained context length (32768), as in Python, instead of 4096. Pass max_context = 4096L to keep the previous behaviour.
  • Golden-fixture tests (tiny checkpoint in tests/fixtures/) now run in every check, with no Python or downloads required.

timestralR 0.1.0

  • Initial native implementation: official fp32 safetensors checkpoints, forward pass and forecasting loop in pure R. Parity vs official PyTorch worst max_rel 2.0e-6 (5M, six cases).
